prompt: Suppose you wanted to run a layer with d = 512 over a whole document of 20,000 tokens instead of a sentence. Using the per-layer costs from Table 1, explain how full self-attention compares with a recurrent layer here, and name the remedy the authors propose for such long inputs.

private.model_answer: Here n is far larger than d, so self-attention's n²·d cost per layer exceeds a recurrent layer's n·d²: comparing all 20,000×20,000 pairs becomes the expensive part. Self-attention still needs only O(1) sequential steps, though. The authors suggest restricting attention to a neighbourhood of size r around each position, which cuts the cost but raises the path length to O(n/r).

rubric.criterion: States that because n is much larger than d, self-attention's per-layer cost (n²·d) is now higher than the recurrent layer's (n·d²)
Names restricting self-attention to a local neighbourhood of size r as the authors' proposed remedy
Notes the trade-off that restricted attention increases the maximum path length to O(n/r)
Notes that self-attention keeps its advantage of O(1) sequential operations
